reasons: The document contains only a narrow Y2K warranty (Section 9) and a self-referential standard of care (Section 11) — neither provides a conformance warranty, workmanlike-services warranty, or any repair/replace/refund/re-performance remedy, so the clause fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies); 'deviation' with an insert is the correct classification per the detection guidance.

The redline is appended to the existing 'TrueLink Warranties' section, which is the natural home, and tracks the model language closely (workmanlike services, conformance to documentation, no malicious code, compliance with laws, vendor-elected repair/replace/refund) without disturbing the surrounding text.
No double-flagging or over-reach: the disclaimer at p0076 already carves out express warranties, so no edit to the disclaimer was needed, and the finding correctly leaves it alone.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, cites the playbook position, and offers the 90/30-day fallback; the 12-month software period sits at the preferred position, which is appropriate for a genuine deviation.
Deterministic checks pass and the changed-character volume is justified because the clause had to be inserted wholesale rather than tweaked.
